Special mention to Mr. Shrikant for his prompt and attentive service, which added to the overall positive experience.

If you're looking for a cozy Chinese dining spot in Dadar with good food and courteous service, Flavours of China is worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Neel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Zen Bowl for lunch to try their food, as I had heard they serve both South Indian and Chinese dishes. My visit was good overall, though not everything was perfect.

When I reached the restaurant, the staff greeted me in a polite way. The place looked clean and comfortable. The menu has many choices, so it is nice if you are going with friends or family who like different types of food.

To start my meal, I ordered a dosa and medu vada. The dosa was crispy and light brown, with a potato filling inside. It was fresh and not very oily. The medu vada was soft and warm, but a little heavy. They served both items with coconut chutney and sambar. The chutney tasted fresh and the sambar was mild. I liked these dishes, but they were not as tasty as what you get in a pure South Indian restaurant. Still, it was good enough for a mixed menu place.

After that, I tried their Chinese food. I ordered vegetable fried rice, Manchurian gravy, and chicken fried rice. The vegetable fried rice had good flavor and plenty of fresh vegetables. It was not too oily, which I liked. The Manchurian was my favorite dish. The sauce was tasty, with a little sweetness and spice, and the vegetable balls were crispy on the outside. The chicken fried rice was also nice, with soft rice and pieces of chicken. The chicken could have had a little more flavor, but it was still enjoyable.

One thing I liked about Zen Bowl is that they have food for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. This makes it easy if you are eating with people who have different food choices. The portions were big enough, and the prices were fair. You get good value for your money here.

The service was friendly, but it was a bit slow. Even though the restaurant was not very crowded, I waited about 10–15 minutes for my food to arrive. The staff were polite and helpful once the food came, but faster service would have made the experience better.

The overall atmosphere was nice. It is a simple place where you can sit comfortably and have a relaxed meal. If you want a fancy restaurant, this may not be the right spot. But if you just want good food at a fair price, Zen Bowl is a decent choice.

I am giving Zen Bowl three stars because the food was fresh and tasty, but nothing was very special or unique. Some dishes were better than others. The Chinese items were definitely the best part of the meal.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
During a recent visit to Yazu Pan Asian Supper Kitchen in Lower Parel, I had the opportunity to indulge in a diverse and flavorful spread that truly showcased the restaurant’s mastery over Asian cuisine. From the moment we arrived, the ambiance set the tone for a relaxed yet upscale dining experience. The service was courteous and efficient, with dishes arriving promptly and plated beautifully.

Our meal began with the Prawn Tempura Roll, which was light, crispy, and paired with just the right balance of sauces. It was followed by the Sriracha Chicken that packed a punch of heat, complemented by a slightly sweet undertone. The Yazu Signature Sichuan Garlic Prawn stood out with its bold flavors and perfectly cooked prawns, a definite must-try for seafood lovers. Another highlight was the Yazu Signature Chicken, which offered a rich and savory profile that paired well with the other mains.

For noodles, the Phad Thai Noodles were enjoyable, with a classic tamarind flavor and the right mix of textures. The Chicken in Hot Garlic Sauce added a spicy, garlicky depth to the meal that was satisfying and comforting. We also tried the Shojo, which added a refreshing and slightly lighter touch to the otherwise intense flavor profile of the dishes.

To end on a sweet note, we ordered the Mathilda Cakes Pull Me Up. It was a delightful dessert that offered a decadent and fun experience, perfectly capping off our evening.

Overall, Yazu delivered a memorable culinary experience with a well-rounded menu and elegant atmosphere. It's a great choice for those looking to explore Pan Asian cuisine with a modern twist in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

featured_reviews.name: Quresh Tyebji

YAZU delivers a standout lunch experience. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely courteous throughout, making the meal feel relaxed and welcoming.

The affogato and cold coffee were an excellent pairing too with the spicy flavors—smooth, rich, and a perfect way to wrap up lunch. A refined yet approachable Pan-Asian spot with fantastic food, strong attention to detail, and great service. Highly recommend.

featured_reviews.name: ADITYA SALVI
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ **DP’s Hotel – A Matunga Classic Opposite Ruia College** ⭐
📍 *Matunga East | Opposite Ruia College*

If you're anywhere near Matunga East and your cravings are leading you towards something delicious, flavorful, and comfortingly local – **DP's Hotel** is a name that *needs* to be on your radar. A long-time favorite among college students, families, and foodies alike, this spot has stood the test of time. I dropped by for a casual evening bite, and here’s the lowdown on my experience.

🍛 **FOOD REVIEW**:

🧈 **Pav Bhaji – 4.5/5**
Easily one of the best in town! Rich, buttery, and full of flavor, it strikes the right balance between spice and tanginess. Served hot with toasted pavs, this dish is a total crowd-pleaser. Definitely a must-try!

🍺 **Fruit Beer – 5/5**
An absolute nostalgic winner. Served chilled, this non-alcoholic classic is a throwback to simpler days. Fizzy, sweet, and perfectly refreshing – it complements the spicy food beautifully.

🍯 **Honey Chilli Plum Potato – 4/5**
A delightful fusion starter. Crispy potatoes tossed in a sticky sweet & spicy glaze, with a hint of plum that sets it apart. Would’ve loved it a tad spicier, but still very satisfying.

🍨 **Gadbad (Mangalore Special Dessert) – 3.5/5**
This colorful layered dessert has all the potential to be a star. However, mine I had whe  the ice cream partially melted – which unfortunately dulled the magic a bit. If you're ordering this, make sure it comes straight from the freezer. That said, the combination of fruits, jelly, nuts, and ice cream is still worth trying once!

🏠 **AMBIENCE & SERVICE**:

DP’s isn’t trying to be a fancy fine-dine, but it delivers big on cleanliness and comfort. The vibe is casual, with fast-moving service and staff that are polite and efficient. It’s the kind of place where you can chill with friends, binge on some desi snacks, and leave with a full heart (and fuller stomach).

✨ **PRO TIPS**:

* **Come early in the evening** to avoid the post-college crowd rush.
* **Grab a seat inside** for a more relaxed dining experience – outdoor seating can get a bit noisy.
* **Try their iconic milkshakes and dosas** if you’re coming back for round two – they’re tasty!

Overall, DP’s is a true **Matunga gem**. Consistent, value-for-money, and packed with flavor. Whether you're a first-timer in the area or a long-time local, this spot deserves a visit – and maybe even a second helping.

---

💬 **Rating: 4.3 / 5 overall**
Would definitely recommend for casual dining, snacking, or those nostalgic food runs with friends.

Chicken Malai Tikka (3/5): The flavor was nice and well-marinated, but the chicken wasn’t as soft and tender as expected.

Chicken Nalli Nihari (3/5): The gravy tasted good and rich, but unfortunately the bone marrow pieces had a slightly weird smell and taste, which affected the overall experience.

Mutton Biryani (3/5): Very heavy on masala with lots of mixed flavors — decent, but a bit overwhelming.

Overall, an average dining experience that could be improved in terms of quality consistency and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: NAFIS AHMED
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Must-Visit for Nihari Lovers on Mohammed Ali Road!!
Chinese and Grill Nalli Nihari on Mohammed Ali Road is an absolute delight for food lovers. The Nalli Nihari is the true star—rich, aromatic, slow-cooked to perfection, and bursting with deep, authentic flavors. The meat is incredibly tender and the gravy is thick, soulful, and perfectly spiced, making every bite satisfying.
The other items are equally impressive, fresh, well-cooked, and generously portioned. Despite the rush that Mohammed Ali Road is known for, the service is quick and well-managed, and the staff is polite and attentive.
Hygiene is maintained well, prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity, and the overall experience feels truly worth it. If you’re exploring Mohammed Ali Road and craving hearty, flavorful non-veg food, this place should definitely be on your list. Highly recommended!!!
